messages.content: What's the distance in milesfrom the Earth to the Moon?

function.name: calculate_distance
function.description: Calculate the distance between two celestial bodies. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

unit.description: The unit of measurement, default is 'km'.

message.content:
The average distance from the center of the Earth to the center of the Moon is about **384 400 kilometers**.  
Converting that into statute miles gives:

\[
384\,400 \text{ km}\;\times\;\frac{0.621371}{1}\;\text{mile/km}
   \approx 238\,900 \text{ miles}.
\]

So you’re looking at roughly **240 thousand miles** on average—though the actual separation varies between about 225 000 mi at perigee and 251 000 mi at apogee because the lunar orbit is slightly eccentric.
